SIMULACRA is a horror video game that has been highly anticipated by fans of the genre. However, after spending 1 hour playing the game, it has become clear to me that it falls far short of expectations.

One of the most disappointing aspects of SIMULACRA is the lack of polish in the graphics and sound design. The game is supposed to take place in the world of a smartphone, but the graphics are clunky and not at all realistic. The sound design is equally disappointing, with poorly implemented jump scares and music that doesn't fit the tone of the game.

The gameplay itself is also frustrating, with slow load times and confusing puzzles that are more frustrating than enjoyable. The story, which revolves around a missing person and the player's attempt to uncover the truth, is poorly executed and lacks the tension and scares that make a horror game truly effective.

In comparison to other horror games, SIMULACRA falls short in every aspect. The characters are one-dimensional and uninteresting, and the player's options for weapons and actions are limited. Even the in-game purchases feel like a desperate attempt to make up for the overall lack of quality in the game.

In my personal opinion, SIMULACRA is a major disappointment. It fails to deliver on the promise of an immersive horror experience and falls far short of the standard set by other games in the genre. I would not recommend this game to anyone and would give it a rating of 2/10.

Having played "A Normal Lost Phone", the concept of Simulacra isn't anything new to me, however due to this not being a particularly common way of making a game it is a welcome addition to this genre of sorts. 
Simulacra also comes with a couple of different twists compared to what "A Normal Lost Phone" had so it's not complete copy.

The good:
*You are thrown into an interesting story that you have to go through with the help of strangers. Who should you trust? Who should you be weary of? Wel that's the beauty, you don't know and you have to base your judgements on scraps of information that you can find. The story is definitely one of the highlights of this game.
*The gameplay whilst isn't groundbreaking works well for this game and doesn't propose any friction for the player on how to proceed.
*There's a decent bit of replayability in this game if you want to uncover all of the different paths. They also aren't particularly difficult to reach if given enough thought.

The bad:
*The horror elements of this game... Don't get me wrong, I love myself some horror and this game seems like a good candidate for a bit of it, however the way it is implemented in this specific game is forced and cliche.
Build tension through uneasiness, not through awful jumpscares.
*I don't need to be redirected to a webpage with a Discord server every time I finish the game. It is annoying. If I want to join your Discord Ill find a way to do it without it being showed in my face every time.
*For a game with so many branching I feel like it should've had a save system. If you want to get a specific achievement you are forced to replay the whole game. It is remedied by the faster conversations, but I do not want to listen to the same conversation for 7 times just so I can get an achievement.
*The acting leaves some things to be desired. I understand that this is an indie game but the video segments in this game felt somewhat robotic and lifeless.

Overall, Simulacra is a fun and interesting little game, that will not burn a hole in your wallet and will keep you entertained for a day or two. I think its worth giving a try, if you can stand the occasional jumpscare.

This game is a bit annoying. I kinda enjoyed my time with it but it's just not good.

On the plus side: it's got decent social media puzzles and a sufficiently creepy atmosphere, ... and that's about all it has going for it. On the minus side: The writing is terrible, the voice acting is not great, there are several cheap jump scares, and the story itself is awful.

Ooh, the story has multiple endings and I should play again? No thank you, once is enough. I can't see what the game could have to offer besides more weak dialogue and weird railroady decisions.

Spoilers, I guess, but I lost and got the worst ending because I didn't show enough trust in the sleazebag (who was specifically written as a sleazy dude) ALL THE WAY IN THE BEGINNING OF THE GAME. It always bunches my britches when a game does that: "Oh you didn't do a thing when you didn't have all the information yet and you couldn't make an informed decision about it? Sucks to be you, Anna's dead." Oh, and also Taylor, he's dead too. Just because I wouldn't send the sleazy dude a cute selfie of the missing girl and I wasn't sufficiently sad enough about him being caught with his pants down (literally, fuck, it's such a contrived story).

I feel like the game is less about saving Anna and more about how you're supposed to protect the feelings of the two douchebag brodudes. There's only one other recurring character, Anna's best friend, Ashley, who could have been of great help, but the story sidelines her almost immediately and only brings her back to intimate that she's secretly in love with Anna. Again, spoilers, but if you've read this far, I doubt you care. (edit: Reading someone else's review, I just learned that to get the absolute best ending, you have to catfish the best friend and reciprocate her feelings without Anna's consent or Ashley's knowledge. Cool game, bro!)

Anyway, don't bother with this game unless you really want a 5 hour puzzle game with a crappy story.
